excerpt: Why I-16, I-95, Abercorn and DeRenne carry so many Savannah crashes, and what to do if you are injured on one.
keyTakeaways: Savannah's most dangerous highways — I-16 (the "Devil's Highway"), I-95, Abercorn Street, DeRenne Avenue, and I-516 — carry traffic volumes that exceed their design capacity, fueled by Port of Savannah truck traffic and 14 million annual tourists. Georgia's two-year statute of limitations (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, less than 50% at fault) govern how crash victims recover compensation, while federal trucking regulations provide additional grounds for claims against commercial carriers.

faqs.question: What is the most dangerous highway in Savannah, Georgia?
faqs.answer: Interstate 16, nicknamed the "Devil's Highway," is one of Savannah's most dangerous roads due to its history of fatal high-speed collisions, heavy commercial truck traffic from the Port of Savannah, and dangerous interchange areas including the I-16/Chatham Parkway junction that handles over 25,000 vehicles daily.

faqs.question: Why is I-16 called the Devil's Highway?
faqs.answer: Locals nicknamed the Savannah segment of I-16 the "Devil's Highway" because of its well-documented history of fatal collisions. The highway carries a dense mix of commuter traffic, long-haul freight trucks serving the Port of Savannah, and vehicles connecting to I-95, creating dangerous speed differentials and congestion that produce deadly crashes.

faqs.question: Is Abercorn Street dangerous in Savannah?
faqs.answer: Yes. Abercorn Street is consistently the most dangerous road in the City of Savannah. The corridor produces more crashes per mile than any other road in Chatham County due to its enormous traffic volumes, heavy commercial development, and multiple high-crash intersections including White Bluff Road, King George Boulevard, Rio Road, and Victory Drive.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, you have two years from the date of your accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in Georgia. South Carolina allows three years under S.C. Code § 15-3-530. Because I-95 crosses the state line, victims of crashes near the Georgia-South Carolina border should be aware of both deadlines.

faqs.question: What should I do after a highway crash on I-16 or I-95 in Savannah?
faqs.answer: Move to safety if possible, call 911 immediately, seek medical treatment even for seemingly minor injuries, document the scene with photographs if safe, do not discuss fault with anyone at the scene, and contact a Savannah car accident lawyer before giving recorded statements to insurance companies. Highway crash evidence can disappear quickly, so prompt legal consultation is critical.

faqs.question: Can I sue a trucking company if their driver caused my crash on I-16 or I-95?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a commercial truck driver's negligence — including fatigue, distraction, impairment, or violation of federal hours-of-service regulations — caused your crash, you may have claims against both the driver and the trucking company. Trucking companies can be held liable under respondeat superior for their drivers' on-duty negligence, and separate claims may arise from the company's own failures in hiring, training, or vehicle maintenance.
